predecessors.note: "He established the State of Alwar in 1775"; Pratap Singh "renounced his allegiance to Jaipur" and built a fort at Rajgarh "with Jaipur's permission" (undated); the Jaipur State page: "the Kachwaha chief of Alwar broke away and ... annexed part of Jaipur's eastern territory". The page also has Pratap Singh taking the Alwar fort when the rulers of Bharatpur failed to pay arrears (undated).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives 3,217 square miles (about 8,332 km2) with 2,627 square miles of plains and 590 of hills, the bounds 27 05 to 28 10 N and 76 10 to 77 15 E, and bordering Gurgaon, Bharatpur, Jaipur, Nabha and Patiala; a 51 km circle about Alwar (about 8,200 km2, ratio 1.0) stands in for all years. The page dates no territorial change after the founding (the nizamats of Ramgarh, Tijara and Kishangarh are undated), so the state is drawn as one shape.

ledger.note: 1775: Pratap Singh Naruka establishes Alwar State. "He established the State of Alwar in 1775." The page names no land with the date; the region is my reading from the area and bounds the page gives for the state; Jaipur is the counterpart because Pratap "renounced his allegiance to Jaipur" and the Jaipur State page has the Kachwaha chief of Alwar annexing part of Jaipur's eastern territory (shared with the Jats of Bharatpur, undated there).

region.text: the Alwar State of 3,217 square miles (about 8,300 km2), between 27 05 and 28 10 N and 76 10 and 77 15 E on the page

ledger.note: 18 March 1948: Alwar merges into the Matsya Union. "Alwar State was merged on 18 March 1948 with three other princely states, namely Bharatpur, Dholpur, and Karauli" to form the Matsya Union ("On 15 May 1949, the Matsya Union was merged with Greater Rajasthan"). The Matsya Union page confirms "formed on 18 March 1948 by the merger of four erstwhile princely states". The page says Tej Singh Prabhakar acceded to the Dominion of India after the partition of 1947 (no day).

certainty.note: The page gives an area and bounds but no boundary; the shape is a circle of the 20th-century area.

sources.title: Alwar State
sources.note: Established 1775 by Pratap Singh; treaty with the East India Company 1803 (Bakhtawar Singh); 1857 help at Bharatpur; area 3,217 square miles; merged 18 March 1948 into the Matsya Union.

sources.title: Matsya Union
sources.note: Formed 18 March 1948 from Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli; merged 15 May 1949 into Greater Rajasthan; statehood 26 January 1950; silent on area.

notes: Two pages opened for the dossier (Alwar State, Matsya Union). Two more fetches (Pratap Singh Naruka and Pratap Singh Prabhakar) returned pages that say almost nothing on territory (an undated incursion into Jaipur by Bakhtawar Singh that ended in defeat, an undated treaty brokered by the East India Company that barred political dealings with other states, and Dhai Gaon near Machari as Pratap Singh's first jagir); the same fetch also returned an accession date of 7 April 1949 that matches Jaipur and not Alwar, so those two pages are not cited. Alwar State: "In the year 1803, during the reign of Bakhtawar Singh, Alwar entered into a mutual offensive and defensive alliance of permanent friendship with the East India Company" and was "the first state in Rajputana to enter into permanent treaty relations" (the british-empire dossier should carry the vassal_start from 1803 with counterpart alwar-state, end 1947); in 1857 it assisted the East India Company against the insurgents at Bharatpur. The page gives no capital, no ruler table and no date for Pratap Singh Naruka's rise; the Jaipur State page (jaipur-state dossier) has the eastern loss shared with the Jats of Bharatpur. matsya-union needs a dossier (1948-03 to 1949-05); area of the union not on its page.
